questions.q: What does [p["name"] for p in catalog] give?
options: A new list with the name of every product
questions.explain: Read it as 'a list of p["name"], for each p in the catalog'. The catalog itself doesn't change.

questions.q: In a list comprehension, where does the value you keep go?
questions.explain: [what_to_keep for item in collection if condition]: what you keep comes first.

questions.q: Which comprehension gives the names of products under ₹500?
options: [p["name"] for p in catalog if p["price_paise"] < 500]
[p["name"] for p in catalog if p["price_paise"] < 50000]
[p["name"] if p["price_paise"] < 50000 for p in catalog]
questions.explain: Bazaar stores paise, so ₹500 is 50000. With 500, the shelf is empty (that's the lab's exercise).

questions.q: What does {p["name"]: p["price_paise"] for p in catalog} build?
options: A dict from name to price
questions.explain: Curly brackets with key: value make a dict. Then price_of["Masala Box"] gives 29900 in one step.

questions.q: {p["seller"] for p in catalog} with two Sharma Electronics products gives how many sellers (out of 5 products)?
questions.explain: Curly brackets with a single value make a set, and a set keeps each value once.

questions.q: When should you write a normal loop instead of a comprehension?
options: When you want to DO something (print, save) or need several conditions; comprehensions are for building a collection
Whenever the list has more than 5 items
questions.explain: [print(p) for p in catalog] builds a useless list of None. If it stops reading like a sentence, use a loop.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What's the difference between [... if cond else ... for p in catalog] and [... for p in catalog if cond]?
options: if/else before the for chooses a value for EVERY item; if at the end SKIPS items
The first one is a set
The second one can't use if
questions.explain: Filter = if at the end (no else). Choose a value = a if cond else b, before the for.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why write sum(p["stock"] for p in catalog) without square brackets?
options: It's a generator expression: values are made one at a time, so no whole list is stored in memory
Brackets would make it a dict
questions.explain: With millions of orders, not building the full list saves a lot of memory. The answer is the same.
